title: 115.从大地到星辰，人类如何丈量世界？
title_en: From the Earth to the Stars: How Do We Measure the World?
summary_cn: 从埃拉托斯特尼的影子到红移测距，人类从未站在宇宙之外，却在系统内部用八把「丈量世界的尺子」一层层搭建起从地球周长到宇宙膨胀的完整地图——核心启示是：有限观察 + 可靠关系 + 层层校准，就能在没有上帝视角时理解整体
summary_en: From Eratosthenes' shadows to redshift distance measurement, humans have never stood outside the universe — yet from inside the system we have built a complete map of the cosmos with eight 'rulers for measuring the world,' stacking up the Earth's circumference and the expansion of the universe layer by layer. The core lesson: limited observations plus reliable relationships plus careful calibration lets us grasp the whole without ever having a god's-eye view.

scenes.title_cn: 第一把尺子：影子丈量地球
scenes.title_en: Ruler One: Measuring the Earth with Shadows
scenes.context: 复刻埃拉托斯特尼两千年前用一根杆子测出地球周长的经典实验。语域：casual 科普讲解。
scenes.speak: At noon on the summer solstice, the sun shines straight down the well in Syene, so there's no shadow. At the same moment, a vertical stick in Alexandria casts a shadow. The two places point in different vertical directions, which proves the Earth is a sphere, and the angle at the center of the Earth is about seven point two degrees — that is, one fiftieth of a full circle. You don't need to walk around the whole planet. A locally measurable phenomenon plus a reasonable model turns a whole-world question into a geometry problem. This is the same family as triangulation and parallax — small angles give long distances. Under parallel sunlight, the two shadows should match; the reality of one side having no shadow at all overturns the flat-Earth assumption. An ordinary person just sees where the sun is; a scientist sees curvature and a center angle.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：夏至正午，塞伊尼（阿斯旺）太阳直射井底无影，亚历山大港同一时刻立杆有影。两地垂直方向不同 → 地球是球体 → 地心角约 7.2°，即 1/50 圆周
sentences.en: Core mechanism: at noon on the summer solstice, the sun shines directly down the well in Syene, so there's no shadow; at the same moment a stick in Alexandria casts one. The two places face different directions, so the Earth must be a sphere — the center angle is about 7.2 degrees, or 1/50 of a full circle.
sentences.note: 表达提示summer solstice → 夏至；cast a shadow → 投影；sphere → 球体；center angle → 地心角

sentences.cn: 关键理解：不需要绕地球走一圈，局部可测现象（影子角度）+ 合理模型（球体 + 平行阳光）→ 整体尺度问题转化为几何问题
sentences.en: Key insight: you don't have to walk around the whole Earth — a locally measurable phenomenon (shadow angle) plus a reasonable model (sphere plus parallel sunlight) turns a whole-world scale problem into geometry.
sentences.note: 表达提示key insight → 关键理解；locally measurable → 局部可测；geometry problem → 几何问题

sentences.cn: 典型场景：任何「无法直接测量整体，但可测局部差异」的尺度问题，都可借鉴此思路
sentences.en: Typical scenario: any scale problem where you can't measure the whole directly but can measure local differences can borrow this approach.
sentences.note: 表达提示scale problem → 尺度问题；borrow this approach → 借鉴此思路；local difference → 局部差异

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据：「局部的影子角度，可以对应到整个地球的原周……你不需要把整个地球走完，你只需要找到一个可以被测量的局部的现象」
sentences.en: Direct quote: 'A local shadow angle can map onto the whole circumference of the Earth... you don't need to walk the entire Earth, you just need to find a local phenomenon you can measure.'
sentences.note: 表达提示circumference → 周长；local phenomenon → 局部现象；map onto → 对应到

sentences.cn: （引用）相关概念：与三角测量、视差法同属「小角度推大距离」几何家族
sentences.en: Related concept: this belongs to the same geometric family as triangulation and parallax — small angles yield long distances.
sentences.note: 表达提示triangulation → 三角测量；parallax → 视差；yield → 得出

sentences.cn: 平行光照射下，两地影子应一致；现实是一边无影一边有影 → 推翻平地假设。同一现象，普通人只见太阳方位，科学家看到曲率与地心角
sentences.en: Under parallel sunlight, the two shadows should match; the reality of one side having no shadow at all overturns the flat-Earth assumption. Same phenomenon: ordinary people see the sun's position, scientists see curvature and the center angle.
sentences.note: 表达提示overturn an assumption → 推翻假设；flat-Earth → 地平说；curvature → 曲率

paraphrase.intent: 想说「不绕地球一圈也能测出地球周长」
phrases: You can measure the whole Earth without walking around it.
A small local measurement can reveal the size of the planet.
paraphrase.chunks: measure the whole · reveal the size of the planet
paraphrase.usage: 第一句直白，第二句更有画面感

paraphrase.intent: 想说「同一现象，外行看热闹内行看门道」
phrases: A tourist sees the sun's position; a scientist sees geometry.
Same shadow, two completely different readings.
paraphrase.chunks: tourist vs scientist · two different readings
paraphrase.usage: 第一句对比结构，第二句更简短口语

scenes.title_cn: 第二把尺子：时间丈量经度
scenes.title_en: Ruler Two: Measuring Longitude with Time
scenes.context: 讲航海时代如何用航海钟把「时间差」变成「经度差」。语域：casual 科普 + 工程故事。
scenes.speak: Latitude is easy: measure the height of a star or the midday sun with a sextant. Longitude has no obvious height to measure — the trick is comparing your local noon with the reference place, Greenwich. One hour equals about fifteen degrees of longitude. The Earth's rotation turns a time difference into a space difference. A marine chronometer looks like it's keeping time, but it's actually doing navigation — it converts time gaps into spatial gaps. GPS does the same thing: signal travel time gives distance. Building that clock was pure engineering grind: no pendulums that rock with the ship, temperature compensation so different metals cancel out expansion, and less friction. The H4 ended up the size of a pocket watch yet met the precision requirement — like a modern MVP iterated release by release.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：纬度靠天体高度（北极星/正午太阳 + 六分仪）易测；经度无直观高度变化，核心是比较本地正午与基准地（格林尼治）的时间差——1 小时 ≈ 15° 经度
sentences.en: Core mechanism: latitude is easy — measure the altitude of a star or the midday sun with a sextant. Longitude has no obvious height change, so the key is comparing local noon with a reference place (Greenwich): 1 hour ≈ 15 degrees of longitude.
sentences.note: 表达提示latitude/longitude → 纬度/经度；sextant → 六分仪；local noon → 本地正午；reference place → 基准地

sentences.cn: 关键理解：地球自转把「时间差」变成「空间差」；航海钟表面计时，实际在定位
sentences.en: Key insight: the Earth's rotation turns a 'time difference' into a 'space difference.' The marine chronometer looks like it's telling time, but it's actually navigating.
sentences.note: 表达提示marine chronometer → 航海钟；turn A into B → 把A变成B；time vs space difference → 时差与空差

sentences.cn: 典型场景：海上无地标导航、任何需要「远程时间同步」的定位系统（GPS 同理）
sentences.en: Typical scenario: navigating at sea with no landmarks — any positioning system that needs remote time sync works the same way, and GPS is no exception.
sentences.note: 表达提示landmark → 地标；time sync → 时间同步；no exception → 同理

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据：「航海钟表面上在计时，它实际上是在定位，它是把时间差换成了空间差」
sentences.en: Direct quote: 'A marine chronometer appears to be telling time; it is actually positioning — it trades a time difference for a space difference.'
sentences.note: 表达提示trade A for B → 用A换取B；positioning → 定位

sentences.cn: （引用）相关概念：与 GPS 信号传播时间测距、雷达测行星距离共享「时间 ↔ 空间」底层逻辑
sentences.en: Related concept: GPS ranging by signal travel time and radar measuring planet distances share the same underlying 'time ↔ space' logic.
sentences.note: 表达提示ranging → 测距；underlying logic → 底层逻辑；radar → 雷达

sentences.cn: 不依赖钟摆（船晃）、设计温度补偿（不同金属膨胀抵消）、减少摩擦——工程化逐点改进，H4 接近怀表体积却达精度要求。类比现代 MVP 迭代发布
sentences.en: No pendulums (the ship rocks), temperature compensation (different metals cancel out expansion), less friction — engineering improved point by point until the H4, nearly pocket-watch size, met the precision target. A good analogy is iterating an MVP release by release.
sentences.note: 表达提示temperature compensation → 温度补偿；cancel out → 相互抵消；point by point → 逐点改进；MVP iteration → 最小可行产品迭代

paraphrase.intent: 想说「航海钟表面在计时，实际在定位」
phrases: The clock looks like it's keeping time, but it's really fixing your position.
Every tick was a measurement of where you were.
paraphrase.chunks: keeping time vs fixing position · every tick is a measurement
paraphrase.usage: 第一句直接点破，第二句更有文学感

paraphrase.intent: 想说「工程是靠一点一点改进堆出来的」
phrases: It was engineering won one detail at a time.
Each small fix moved the needle until it worked.
paraphrase.chunks: one detail at a time · move the needle
paraphrase.usage: 第一句中性陈述，第二句用习语 move the needle 更有力

scenes.title_cn: 第三把尺子：三角网与 GPS
scenes.title_en: Ruler Three: Triangulation Networks and GPS
scenes.context: 从国家大地原点到三角测量控制网，再到手机里的 GPS 卫星定位。语域：casual 科普 + 测绘故事。
scenes.speak: A country's geodetic origin — like the seven-ton granite marker in Jingyang, Shaanxi — gets its absolute coordinates from astronomical observation. Then a baseline is laid, triangulation extends a control network, and rivers, roads, and villages all hang onto that skeleton. Coordinates are just numbers; the real world doesn't carry labels, so you have to map it into a unified reference frame like WGS84 first. This shows up in national surveying and urban construction, and those round metal benchmark disks are still legally protected today. For large areas you need the ellipsoid model, and different datums give different coordinates for the same place. The round metal disk with an engraved number on the roadside is a physical relic of a triangulation node. And GPS: your phone picks up multiple satellites at once; each tells you its position and the time it sent the signal — speed of light times travel time equals distance. One satellite limits you to a sphere; three intersect at a point; a fourth corrects your clock error.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：国家大地原点（如陕西泾阳 7 吨花岗岩标石）经天文观测得绝对经纬度 → 引出基准边 AB → 三角测量扩展控制网 → 河流道路村庄挂靠骨架
sentences.en: Core mechanism: the national geodetic origin — such as the 7-ton granite marker in Jingyang, Shaanxi — gets its absolute coordinates from astronomical observation, a baseline AB is laid out, triangulation extends a control network, and rivers, roads, and villages are hung onto that skeleton.
sentences.note: 表达提示geodetic origin → 大地原点；baseline → 基准边；control network → 控制网；hang onto → 挂靠

sentences.cn: 关键理解：经纬度是数字，地上不会写着坐标；必须先把真实世界映射进统一参考系（如 WGS84）
sentences.en: Key insight: coordinates are just numbers — the ground doesn't come with labels written on it; you first have to map the real world into a unified reference frame like WGS84.
sentences.note: 表达提示reference frame → 参考系；map into → 映射进；WGS84 → 全球坐标系统

sentences.cn: 典型场景：国土测绘、城市基建、现代「国家水准点」圆形金属片仍受法律保护
sentences.en: Typical scenario: national surveying, urban infrastructure — and the round metal 'national levelbenchmarks' you see on streets are still protected by law.
sentences.note: 表达提示surveying → 测绘；benchmark disk → 水准点圆盘；protected by law → 受法律保护

sentences.cn: 适用边界：大范围须考虑地球椭球（参考椭球 + 大地基准），不同基准系下同一地点经纬度会有差异
sentences.en: Boundary: over large areas you must account for the Earth's ellipsoid — the reference ellipsoid plus the geodetic datum — and the same location has different coordinates under different datums.
sentences.note: 表达提示ellipsoid → 椭球体；geodetic datum → 大地基准；account for → 考虑

sentences.cn: （引用）怎么落地：路上见到刻编号的圆形金属水准点，即三角网节点的物理遗存
sentences.en: How to apply it: a round metal benchmark disk engraved with a number by the roadside is the physical relic of a triangulation node.
sentences.note: 表达提示engraved → 刻有编号的；physical relic → 物理遗存；triangulation node → 三角网节点

sentences.cn: 核心机制：手机同时收多颗卫星信号；每颗卫星告知位置 + 信号发出时间 → 光速 × 传播时间 = 距离 → 一颗卫星限定球面，三颗交会定一点，第四颗修正时钟误差
sentences.en: Core mechanism: the phone receives signals from several satellites at once; each reports its position and the time it sent the signal — speed of light times travel time equals distance. One satellite confines you to a sphere, three intersect at a point, and a fourth corrects the clock error.
sentences.note: 表达提示speed of light → 光速；travel time → 传播时间；intersect → 交会；clock error → 时钟误差

paraphrase.intent: 想说「世界本身不标坐标，要先建立参照系」
phrases: The world doesn't come with coordinates printed on it.
You have to build a reference frame before you can locate anything.
paraphrase.chunks: coordinates printed · build a reference frame
paraphrase.usage: 第一句形象，第二句偏方法论

paraphrase.intent: 想说「四颗卫星才能修正时钟误差」
phrases: Three satellites give you a point; the fourth fixes your clock.
That extra satellite is what makes GPS precise.
paraphrase.chunks: three give a point, fourth fixes the clock · makes GPS precise
paraphrase.usage: 第一句讲机制，第二句做结论

scenes.title_cn: 第四至五把尺子：视差丈量宇宙距离
scenes.title_en: Rulers Four & Five: Parallax Across the Universe
scenes.context: 从金星凌日解锁太阳系，到贝塞尔用视差把恒星距离带入定量时代。语域：casual 天文科普。
scenes.speak: With a known baseline and an observed angle difference, a triangle gives you the distance. During a transit of Venus, observers north and south of the Earth see the black dot cross the sun on slightly different paths — that yields the Earth-Venus distance, and combined with Kepler's orbital ratios (Earth 1, Venus 0.72) it unlocks the whole solar system in kilometers, defining one astronomical unit. Kepler's laws give you the proportional map; parallax gives you the absolute scale; only together do you get one AU equals 150 million kilometers. The baseline is the limit: the Earth's diameter works for the solar system, but stars need a bigger baseline. So the baseline expands from one Earth diameter to two AU — about 300 million kilometers. In the nineteenth century Bessel measured the parallax of 61 Cygni at less than one arcsecond — the angle of a coin seen from a few kilometers away — and star distances entered the quantitative era. As the hosts said, failing to measure parallax doesn't mean the Earth isn't moving; it just means the instruments aren't precise enough yet. And the transit itself is fragile: Venus touching the sun's edge stretches and sticks, making the exact moment hard to judge, and a cloudy day wastes years of preparation.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：已知基线长度 + 观测角度差 → 三角形确定距离。金星凌日：地球上南北观测者看到黑点路径不同 → 得地火距离 → 结合开普勒轨道比例（地球 1，金星 0.72）解锁整个太阳系公里数 → 定义 1 天文单位
sentences.en: Core mechanism: known baseline plus observed angle difference → a triangle fixes the distance. During a transit of Venus, observers north and south on Earth see the black dot's path shift, giving the Earth-Venus distance; combined with Kepler's orbital ratios (Earth = 1, Venus = 0.72) this unlocks the solar system in kilometers and defines 1 astronomical unit.
sentences.note: 表达提示transit of Venus → 金星凌日；orbital ratio → 轨道比例；astronomical unit → 天文单位

sentences.cn: 关键理解：开普勒定律给比例地图，视差法给绝对标尺；二者结合才有一 AU = 1.5 亿公里
sentences.en: Key insight: Kepler's laws provide a proportional map; parallax provides the absolute scale; only the two together yield 1 AU = 150 million kilometers.
sentences.note: 表达提示proportional map → 比例地图；absolute scale → 绝对标尺；yield → 得出

sentences.cn: 适用边界：基线有限——地球直径测太阳系够用，测恒星则需更大基线
sentences.en: Boundary: the baseline is limited — the Earth's diameter suffices for the solar system, but measuring stars requires a larger baseline.
sentences.note: 表达提示baseline → 基线；suffice for → 够用；require → 需要

sentences.cn: 基线从地球直径扩展到 2 AU（约 3 亿公里）。贝塞尔 19 世纪测天鹅座 61 星视差 < 1 角秒（约几公里外看硬币的夹角）→ 恒星距离进入定量时代
sentences.en: The baseline expands from the Earth's diameter to 2 AU (about 300 million km). In the 19th century Bessel measured the parallax of 61 Cygni at under 1 arcsecond — roughly the angle of a coin seen from a few kilometers away — bringing star distances into the quantitative era.
sentences.note: 表达提示arcsecond → 角秒；61 Cygni → 天鹅座61；quantitative era → 定量时代

sentences.cn: （引用）「测不到视差，不是说明地球没有动，只是说明仪器还不够精密」
sentences.en: Direct quote: 'Not detecting parallax doesn't mean the Earth isn't moving — it just means the instruments aren't precise enough yet.'
sentences.note: 表达提示detect parallax → 测到视差；precise enough → 足够精密

sentences.cn: 原因：金星边缘与太阳盘面接触时出现拉伸粘连，难判精确时刻；阴天则数年准备白费
sentences.en: Why it's hard: Venus's edge stretches and sticks to the sun's disk as it touches, making the exact moment hard to judge — and a cloudy day wastes years of preparation.
sentences.note: 表达提示stretch and stick → 拉伸粘连；judge the moment → 判断时刻；waste preparation → 白费准备

paraphrase.intent: 想说「比例地图要配上绝对标尺才完整」
phrases: Ratios alone give you a map without units.
You need both the proportional map and an absolute ruler.
paraphrase.chunks: ratios without units · proportional map and absolute ruler
paraphrase.usage: 第一句讲缺口，第二句讲组合

paraphrase.intent: 想说「测不到不代表不存在，只是工具不够好」
phrases: Failing to measure something doesn't mean it isn't there.
It just means your instruments aren't good enough yet.
paraphrase.chunks: fail to measure vs not there · instruments not good enough
paraphrase.usage: 第一句是完整表述，第二句更口语自然

scenes.title_cn: 第六至七把尺子：标准烛光与距离阶梯
scenes.title_en: Rulers Six & Seven: Standard Candles and the Distance Ladder
scenes.context: 造父变星的周期-光度关系和 Ia 型超新星，如何把测距推到极远星系。语域：casual 天文科普 + 方法论。
scenes.speak: Cepheid variables change brightness in a cycle, and the longer the period, the brighter the star. Measure the period, learn the intrinsic luminosity, compare with the apparent brightness, and the distance follows the inverse-square law — distance is proportional to one over the square root of brightness. Hubble found Cepheids in Andromeda with distances far beyond the Milky Way, confirming that extragalactic galaxies exist and rewriting our sense of cosmic scale. As the episode puts it, nearby methods calibrate distant methods, and distant methods push outward again — cosmic distance measurement has always been built layer by layer. The first rung: parallax calibrates nearby Cepheids, which then reach farther galaxies. Type Ia supernovae are the next rung: a white dwarf accretes matter from a companion until it hits a critical mass and detonates in an uncontrollable thermonuclear explosion; after correcting for the light-curve shape, the peak brightness is fairly consistent and bright enough to see across extremely distant galaxies. But the boundaries are real: in faraway galaxies you can't resolve individual Cepheids, dust absorption adds error, and calibration errors at the bottom propagate up the ladder.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：造父变星亮度周期性变化，周期越长本身越亮。测周期 → 知绝对光度 → 对比视亮度 → 距离 ∝ 1/√亮度（平方反比律）
sentences.en: Core mechanism: Cepheid variables brighten and dim in a cycle — the longer the period, the brighter the star intrinsically. Measure the period → get the absolute luminosity → compare the apparent brightness → distance ∝ 1/√brightness (inverse-square law).
sentences.note: 表达提示Cepheid variable → 造父变星；intrinsic luminosity → 绝对光度；apparent brightness → 视亮度；inverse-square law → 平方反比律

sentences.cn: 关键理解：哈勃在仙女座发现造父变星，距离远超银河系 → 确认河外星系存在，改写宇宙尺度认知
sentences.en: Key insight: Hubble found Cepheids in Andromeda with distances far beyond the Milky Way — confirming extragalactic galaxies exist and rewriting our sense of cosmic scale.
sentences.note: 表达提示Andromeda → 仙女座；extragalactic galaxy → 河外星系；cosmic scale → 宇宙尺度

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据：「进出的方法校准远出的方法，远出的方法再向外扩展……宇宙测距从来都是这样一层一层搭起来的」
sentences.en: Direct quote: 'Near methods calibrate far methods, and far methods push outward again... cosmic distance measurement has always been stacked layer by layer.'
sentences.note: 表达提示calibrate → 校准；push outward → 向外扩展；stack layer by layer → 一层层搭建

sentences.cn: （引用）距离阶梯第一层：视差法校准附近造父变星 → 用于更远星系
sentences.en: The first rung of the distance ladder: parallax calibrates nearby Cepheids, which are then used for more distant galaxies.
sentences.note: 表达提示distance ladder → 距离阶梯；rung → 梯级；nearby → 附近的

sentences.cn: 核心机制：白矮星吸积伴星物质至临界质量热核失控爆炸，峰值亮度经光变曲线形状校正后较一致；亮到可观测极远星系
sentences.en: Core mechanism: a white dwarf accretes matter from a companion star until a critical mass triggers an uncontrollable thermonuclear explosion; after correcting for the light-curve shape, the peak brightness is fairly consistent — and bright enough to observe in extremely distant galaxies.
sentences.note: 表达提示white dwarf → 白矮星；accrete → 吸积；thermonuclear explosion → 热核爆炸；light curve → 光变曲线

sentences.cn: 适用边界：星系太远则无法分辨单颗造父变星；尘埃吸收会增大误差；低层校准误差会传递到高层
sentences.en: Boundary: in galaxies too far away you can't resolve individual Cepheids; dust absorption inflates the error, and calibration errors at the bottom propagate up to higher rungs.
sentences.note: 表达提示resolve → 分辨；dust absorption → 尘埃吸收；propagate → 传递（误差传播）

paraphrase.intent: 想说「用近处的尺子校准远处的尺子」
phrases: You calibrate distant rulers with nearby ones.
Each rung of the ladder is checked by the one below it.
paraphrase.chunks: calibrate distant with nearby · each rung checked by the one below
paraphrase.usage: 第一句直白，第二句更有画面感

paraphrase.intent: 想说「底层误差会逐级放大」
phrases: Errors at the bottom cascade up the ladder.
A small calibration slip grows with every step outward.
paraphrase.chunks: cascade up · slip grows with every step
paraphrase.usage: 第一句是术语，第二句更通俗

scenes.title_cn: 第八把尺子：红移与宇宙膨胀
scenes.title_en: Ruler Eight: Redshift and the Expanding Universe
scenes.context: 红移如何成为宇宙级测距尺，以及「看向远方就是看向过去」。语域：casual 天文科普 + 哲学余味。
scenes.speak: In the lab, the hydrogen spectral line should sit at 656.3 nanometers; in distant galaxies it shows up around 720 — a wholesale redshift. Define z as the change in wavelength over the wavelength; Hubble's law says velocity equals H-naught times distance; and the farther away, the bigger the redshift. As the hosts said, when we look far away we are looking into the past — redshift is both a distance indicator and, at the same time, a time indicator. Galaxies are embedded in space, and space itself is expanding, stretching the light waves. Think of a balloon: every point moves away from every other point, with no center — every observer sees distant galaxies receding. Redshift distance needs a cosmological model: matter density, dark energy, curvature — and Type Ia supernovae calibrate the redshift-distance relationship. This episode stops at redshift; the cosmic microwave background, baryon acoustic oscillations, and gravitational waves are even more technical tools for larger scales.

sentences.cn: 实验室知氢谱线应在 656.3 nm，遥远星系中出现在 720 nm → 整体红移。z = Δλ/λ；哈勃定律 v = H₀ × d。越遥远红移越大
sentences.en: In the lab, the hydrogen line should sit at 656.3 nm; in distant galaxies it appears at 720 nm — a wholesale redshift. z = Δλ/λ; Hubble's law says v = H₀ × d; the more distant, the larger the redshift.
sentences.note: 表达提示spectral line → 谱线；redshift → 红移；wholesale → 整体性的；Hubble's law → 哈勃定律

sentences.cn: （引用）「当我们看向远方，其实就是看向过去……红移既是距离指标，它同时又回到了时间指标」
sentences.en: Direct quote: 'When we look far away, we are actually looking into the past... redshift is a distance indicator that also returns to being a time indicator.'
sentences.note: 表达提示look into the past → 看向过去；distance indicator → 距离指标；time indicator → 时间指标

sentences.cn: 核心机制：星系镶嵌在空间中，空间本身膨胀拉长光波；气球表面各点相互远离，无中心点——每个观测者都见远处星系退行
sentences.en: Core mechanism: galaxies are embedded in space, and space itself is expanding, stretching the light waves. Like a balloon surface, every point recedes from every other — there is no center, and every observer sees distant galaxies receding.
sentences.note: 表达提示embedded in space → 镶嵌在空间中；expand → 膨胀；recede → 退行；no center → 无中心

sentences.cn: 关键理解：红移测距需宇宙学模型（物质密度、暗能量、曲率）；靠 Ia 型超新星距离校准红移-距离关系
sentences.en: Key insight: redshift distance requires a cosmological model (matter density, dark energy, curvature), and Type Ia supernovae calibrate the redshift-distance relationship.
sentences.note: 表达提示cosmological model → 宇宙学模型；dark energy → 暗能量；calibrate → 校准

sentences.cn: 适用边界：本节目止于红移；CMB、BAO、引力波等更大尺度工具更技术流
sentences.en: Boundary: the episode stops at redshift — the cosmic microwave background, baryon acoustic oscillations, and gravitational waves are even more technical tools for larger scales.
sentences.note: 表达提示cosmic microwave background → 宇宙微波背景；baryon acoustic oscillations → 重子声学振荡；gravitational waves → 引力波

paraphrase.intent: 想说「看远方就是看过去」
phrases: The farther you look, the further back in time you see.
Distance and time are the same direction in astronomy.
paraphrase.chunks: the farther, the further back · distance and time align
paraphrase.usage: 第一句直白，第二句更凝练

phrases: The universe has no center to expand from.
Every observer is the center of their own sky.
paraphrase.chunks: no center · center of their own sky
paraphrase.usage: 第一句是结论，第二句更有诗意

scenes.title_cn: 科学思维：系统内部的丈量
scenes.title_en: Scientific Thinking: Measuring From Inside the System
scenes.context: 把八把尺子上升为方法论：有限观察 + 可靠关系 + 层层校准。语域：casual 科普总结 + 哲思。
scenes.speak: Humans have never stood outside the Earth, outside the solar system, or outside the universe. We only have local, limited observations — shadows, starlight, the ticking of clocks. The relationships must be stable, verifiable, and cross-checkable against other facts; you can't skip the lower rungs of calibration and trust the higher inferences directly. As the hosts put it, science's real power is that it doesn't demand all the answers up front — it finds reliable relationships within limited observations. In practice: when you face a big problem, find a measurable local quantity, build a model relationship, then extrapolate layer by layer and cross-validate. And far from dimming the stars, understanding the distance, time, elements, and expansion behind each beam of light makes the night sky richer. Light from four and a half billion light-years away is what that world looked like four and a half billion years ago — behind every beam of starlight there are endless stories.

sentences.cn: 为什么重要：人类从未站在地球外、太阳系外、宇宙外；只有局部、有限的观察——影子、星光、钟表的滴答
sentences.en: Why it matters: humans have never stood outside the Earth, the solar system, or the universe — we only have local, limited observations: shadows, starlight, the ticking of clocks.
sentences.note: 表达提示stand outside the system → 站在系统之外；limited observation → 有限的观察；ticking of clocks → 钟表滴答

sentences.cn: 适用边界：关系必须稳定、可验证、能与其他事实互证；不能跳过低层校准直接信任高层推论
sentences.en: Boundary: the relationships must be stable, verifiable, and mutually confirmable with other facts; you can't skip lower-level calibration and trust higher-level inferences directly.
sentences.note: 表达提示verifiable → 可验证的；mutually confirmable → 互相印证；skip calibration → 跳过校准；inference → 推论

sentences.cn: （引用）「科学真正厉害的地方就在于，它不要求我们一开始就拥有全部答案……在有限的观察里找出可靠的关系」
sentences.en: Direct quote: 'What science is truly great at is that it doesn't demand that we have all the answers from the start... it finds reliable relationships within limited observations.'
sentences.note: 表达提示have all the answers → 拥有全部答案；reliable relationship → 可靠关系；from the start → 一开始

sentences.cn: （引用）怎么落地：遇到大问题，先找可测量的局部量，建立模型关系，再层层外推并交叉验证
sentences.en: How to apply it: when facing a big problem, first find a measurable local quantity, establish a model relationship, then extrapolate layer by layer and cross-validate.
sentences.note: 表达提示measurable local quantity → 可测量的局部量；establish a model → 建立模型；extrapolate → 外推；cross-validate → 交叉验证

sentences.cn: 恰恰相反：了解每束光背后的距离、时间、元素与膨胀故事，星空反而更丰富。45 亿光年外的光，是那颗星球 45 亿年前的样子
sentences.en: Quite the opposite: understanding the distance, time, elements, and expansion story behind each beam of light makes the starry sky richer. Light from 4.5 billion light-years away is what that world looked like 4.5 billion years ago.
sentences.note: 表达提示quite the opposite → 恰恰相反；light-year → 光年；starry sky → 星空

sentences.cn: （引用）「每一束星光背后都有无穷多的故事」
sentences.en: Direct quote: 'Behind every beam of starlight there are endless stories.'
sentences.note: 表达提示beam of starlight → 一束星光；endless stories → 无穷无尽的故事

paraphrase.intent: 想说「不必站在系统外也能理解整体」
phrases: You don't need a god's-eye view to understand the whole.
From inside the system, careful measurement still reveals the big picture.
paraphrase.chunks: god's-eye view · inside the system, measure the big picture
paraphrase.usage: 第一句是核心命题，第二句展开细节

paraphrase.intent: 想说「了解背后的故事让星空更美」
phrases: Knowing the science makes the night sky more beautiful, not less.
Every star is richer once you know its story.
paraphrase.chunks: more beautiful, not less · richer once you know its story
paraphrase.usage: 第一句驳斥误解，第二句温和总结

practice.cn: 用「turn A into B」说：地球自转把时间差变成空间差。
practice.en: The Earth's rotation turns a time difference into a space difference.

practice.cn: 用「cancel out」说：不同金属膨胀相互抵消。
practice.en: Different metals expand and cancel each other out.

practice.cn: 用「layer by layer」说：宇宙测距是一层层搭起来的。
practice.en: Cosmic distance measurement is built layer by layer.

practice.cn: 用「map onto」说：局部影子角度可以对应到整个地球周长。
practice.en: A local shadow angle can map onto the whole circumference of the Earth.

pitfalls.wrong: The shadow proves Earth is a ball.
pitfalls.right: The shadow angle proves the Earth is a sphere.
pitfalls.why: 口语里 ball 能懂，但科普语境用 sphere 更准确正式。

pitfalls.wrong: The clock is used to position.
pitfalls.right: The clock is actually navigating — it fixes your position.
pitfalls.why: used to do 表习惯动作；此处是「实际在做定位」，用 is actually doing / is used for positioning。

pitfalls.wrong: The GPS satellite tells us where is the distance.
pitfalls.right: Each satellite reports its position and the signal's send time, and distance is light speed times travel time.
pitfalls.why: GPS 测距靠时间而非直接告诉你距离；中文直译会造成概念错误。

pitfalls.wrong: The farther star has bigger shift, so it moves faster.
pitfalls.right: A larger redshift means a greater distance — the expansion itself stretches the light.
pitfalls.why: 是空间膨胀拉长光波，不是星星在狂奔；要区分「视退行速度」与「空间膨胀」。

shifts.before: 以为要「绕地球一圈」才能知道地球多大
shifts.after: 局部可测的现象 + 合理模型，就能推出整体尺度

shifts.before: 以为科学与美感是对立的，懂了原理星空就变无聊
shifts.after: 了解每束光背后的距离、时间与故事，星空反而更丰富

shifts.before: 以为精确测量靠的是更贵更大的仪器
shifts.after: 靠的是层层校准的链条——低层误差会逐级放大到高层
